newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian silver recovers at close, gold steady.
newsitem.headline: Indian silver recovers at close, gold steady.

text.p: ** Standard gold 24 carats was steady at 4,750 rupees per 10 grammes. It lost 20 rupees per 10 grammes on Tuesday on weak world prices, a trend unchanged on Wednesday.
** Gold biscuits (116.50 grammes) also closed steady at 55,500 rupees per piece.
** Silver.999 recovered to close five rupees higher at 6,735 rupees per kg on improved buying. It opened 15 rupees lower at 6,715 rupees per kg on higher arrivals and a weak world trend.
Silver recovered on improved buying to close 5.0 rupees higher at 6,735 rupees per kg, dealers said.
It opened weak at 6,715 rupees per kg, 15 rupees down on higher arrivals and a weak world trend.
"The overall market trend is weak, mainly because of good supplies and subdued world prices despite good local demand," said leading bullion dealer Bhayabhai Sanghavi.
Standard gold 24 carats closed steady at 4,750 rupees per 10 grammes with demand matching supply.
"Imports of gold by Indian expatriates have been good," said Sanghavi. "The flow has been steady, though it's difficult to estimate the quantiy."
Sanghavi said Indian expatriates and traders who imported gold using special import licenses (SILs), were taking advantage of a dip in world prices.
Indian expatriates, a large number of them employees in Gulf countries, are allowed to bring in up to 10 kgs of gold once every six months, subject to a duty of 220 rupees per 10 grammes.
India also allows bullion dealers and other traders to import gold using SILs which are issued against foreign exchange earnings and traded openly.
Gold biscuits (116.50 grammes) also closed steady at 55,500 rupees per piece. (Conversion $1=35.77 rupees)
